prompt: The angles of a triangle measure $(2x)°$, $(3x + 10)°$, and $(x - 10)°$. What is the value of $x$?
hint: Set the sum of the three expressions equal to $180$.

hints.text: Set the sum of the three expressions equal to $180$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try simpler expressions: angles $x$, $x$, and $x$ give $3x = 180$, so $x = 60$. Sum all three expressions, set the total to $180$, and solve.

learningObjective: Solve for a variable using the triangle angle sum.
explanation: The three angles sum to $180°$: $2x + 3x + 10 + x - 10 = 180$.
Combine like terms — the $+10$ and $-10$ cancel: $6x = 180$.
$x = 30$. The angles are $60°$, $100°$, and $20°$, which do sum to $180$ ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Finish by checking, not by stopping
steps: The question asked for $x$, which is $30$ — not for an angle measure.
But computing the three angles anyway is a fast, complete verification.
If they had not summed to $180$, you would know immediately that the algebra went wrong.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: 60 — the first angle, 2x — is the offered near-miss for anyone who forgets what was asked.
The question wants x itself. Solve, then re-read the stem; computing all three angles as a check also reminds you which quantity to report.
